# package client

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/client"
```

Package client implements the controlling station (master) of IEC 60870-5-104.

A [Client](#type-client) owns one connection to a controlled station. It runs the protocol machine (sequence numbers, acknowledgements, the t1/t2/t3 timers and the k/w windows), delivers every received ASDU to a [Handler](#type-handler) and offers the application functions of the standard as blocking calls:

	c, err := client.Dial(ctx, "10.0.0.5:2404",
		client.WithHandler(client.HandlerFunc(func(a *asdu.ASDU) {
			fmt.Println(a)
		})))
	if err != nil { ... }
	defer c.Close()

	points, err := c.Interrogate(ctx, 1, asdu.QOIStation)
	err = c.Command(ctx, 1, asdu.SingleCommand{IOA: 6001, Value: true})
	log, err := c.GetFile(ctx, 1, 30000, 1)

All methods are safe for concurrent use.

Client is the controlling station end of one IEC 60870-5-104 connection. Create it with [New](#func-new) or [Dial](#func-dial). It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Client) ClockSync

```go
func (c *Client) ClockSync(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, t time.Time) error
```

ClockSync sets the clock of the station to t (C\_CS\_NA\_1) and waits for the confirmation. The time is sent in the zone of the ASDU parameters, UTC by default.

#### func (Client) Close

```go
func (c *Client) Close() error
```

Close closes the connection and stops reconnecting. Pending requests fail with [iec104.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrClosed). When Close returns the [Handler](#type-handler) and the state handler have been called for the last time: a call in progress has returned and none follows. Before that the Handler is given what the connection had received, and acknowledged to the station, up to the moment of the call.

Called from the Handler or the state handler, Close cannot wait for that call: it returns at once, the Handler is not called again, and "disconnected" is reported after the call has returned. Close is idempotent; every caller outside a callback returns when the client is closed.

#### func (Client) Command

```go
func (c *Client) Command(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, obj asdu.InformationObject) error
```

Command sends a process command with cause "activation" and waits for the activation confirmation. obj must be one of [asdu.SingleCommand](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#SingleCommand), [asdu.DoubleCommand](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#DoubleCommand), [asdu.StepCommand](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#StepCommand), [asdu.SetpointNormalized](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#SetpointNormalized), [asdu.SetpointScaled](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#SetpointScaled), [asdu.SetpointFloat](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#SetpointFloat) or [asdu.BitstringCommand](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#BitstringCommand). A command whose Time is set is sent as the CP56Time2a variant.

A negative confirmation or an "unknown ..." answer is returned as [\*iec104.NegativeError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#NegativeError).

For select-before-operate call Command twice: first with Select set, then without. The activation termination some stations send after executing is not awaited; it reaches the [Handler](#type-handler).

#### func (Client) Connect

```go
func (c *Client) Connect(ctx context.Context) error
```

Connect establishes the transport connection and, unless disabled with [WithAutoStart](#func-withautostart), starts data transfer. The connection attempt is bounded by ctx and by t0, whichever is shorter.

Connect fails with [iec104.ErrBusy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrBusy) when the client is already connected or connecting. With [WithReconnect](#func-withreconnect) it only needs to succeed once: the client re-establishes a lost connection by itself.

#### func (Client) CounterInterrogate

```go
func (c *Client) CounterInterrogate(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, request, freeze uint8) ([]*asdu.ASDU, error)
```

CounterInterrogate runs a counter interrogation (C\_CI\_NA\_1) and collects the integrated totals the station sends in answer, until the activation termination arrives. request is [asdu.CounterGeneral](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#CounterGeneral) or a counter group 1..4; freeze is one of the asdu.Freeze\* qualifiers.

It follows the same collection rules as [Client.Interrogate](#func-client-interrogate).

```go
func (c *Client) Deactivate(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, obj asdu.InformationObject) error
```

Deactivate cancels a previously selected command: it sends obj with cause "deactivation" and waits for the deactivation confirmation.

#### func (Client) GetFile

```go
func (c *Client) GetFile(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, ioa asdu.IOA, name uint16) ([]byte, error)
```

GetFile downloads a file from the controlled station: the file transfer procedure in monitor direction (IEC 60870-5-101, 7.4.11). ioa is the information object address of the file and name its name of file (NOF).

It selects and calls the file, then calls every section the station announces, checks the length and the checksum of each section and of the file, and acknowledges them. It returns the content once the file is acknowledged.

A station that refuses the file (unknown address or name, file not ready) is reported as [\*iec104.NegativeError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#NegativeError). A length or checksum that does not match is acknowledged negatively and reported as [iec104.ErrProtocol](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrProtocol).

The request timeout bounds every wait for the station, not the whole transfer; ctx bounds the transfer. The ASDUs of the transfer are also delivered to the [Handler](#type-handler). Two transfers of the same file at once fail with [iec104.ErrBusy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrBusy), and a download is never repeated by [WithRetry](#func-withretry).

#### func (Client) Interrogate

```go
func (c *Client) Interrogate(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, qoi asdu.QOI) ([]*asdu.ASDU, error)
```

Interrogate runs an interrogation (C\_IC\_NA\_1): it sends the command, waits for the confirmation and collects the ASDUs the station sends with the matching "interrogated by ..." cause until the activation termination arrives.

qoi is [asdu.QOIStation](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#QOIStation) for a general interrogation or [asdu.QOIGroup](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#QOIGroup)(n) for one group. With ca set to [asdu.Broadcast](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#Broadcast) the answers of all stations are collected until the first termination.

The collected ASDUs are also delivered to the [Handler](#type-handler). A large station can take longer than the default request timeout: pass a context with a suitable deadline. On error the ASDUs collected so far are returned alongside it.

#### func (Client) ListFiles

```go
func (c *Client) ListFiles(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, ioa asdu.IOA) ([]asdu.FileDirectoryEntry, error)
```

ListFiles calls the directory of the controlled station (F\_SC\_NA\_1 with cause "request") and returns its entries (F\_DR\_TA\_1), collected until the entry the station marks as the last one ([asdu.FileLastOfDirectory](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#FileLastOfDirectory)). ioa selects a directory; 0 is the station's default one.

A station without a directory answers with the mirrored call, which is reported as [\*iec104.NegativeError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#NegativeError).

#### func (Client) PutFile

```go
func (c *Client) PutFile(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, ioa asdu.IOA, name uint16, sections ...[]byte) error
```

PutFile sends a file to the controlled station: the file transfer procedure in control direction. ioa is the information object address of the file and name its name of file (NOF). Every argument after that is one section; a section is sent in segments of up to [asdu.MaxSegmentLength](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#MaxSegmentLength) octets. Without sections an empty file is sent.

It announces the file, answers the station's calls for the file and for each section with the data and its checksum, and returns once the station has acknowledged the file.

A station that refuses the file, or answers a section or the file with a negative acknowledgement, is reported as [\*iec104.NegativeError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#NegativeError). The request timeout bounds every wait for the station, ctx the transfer as a whole. A transfer is never repeated by [WithRetry](#func-withretry).

#### func (Client) Read

```go
func (c *Client) Read(ctx context.Context, ca asdu.CommonAddr, ioa asdu.IOA) (*asdu.ASDU, error)
```

Read requests the current value of one information object (C\_RD\_NA\_1) and returns the ASDU the station sends with cause "request" for that address. An unknown address is reported as [\*iec104.NegativeError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#NegativeError).

#### func (Client) Send

```go
func (c *Client) Send(ctx context.Context, a *asdu.ASDU) error
```

Send transmits one ASDU without waiting for any answer. It blocks while the send window is full (k unacknowledged I frames). Use the request methods for the standard application functions; Send is for everything else, such as deactivations, parameters, file transfer and private types.

### type Group

```go
type Group struct {

	// mu serializes reconcile and Switchover. It is held across STARTDT and
	// STOPDT, which wait for the station, and never across a callback of
	// the application: those may call the group.

	// stateMu guards started and closed and is never held across a call
	// that blocks, so that Close can be called from anywhere.

	// ends when the group is closed

	// A connection that was never established, or whose first attempt
	// failed, is dialed by the group, with the delays of [WithReconnect].

	// The switch handler is called outside mu, one call at a time and in
	// order, so that it may call back into the group.

	// goroutine calling the switch handler, 0 when idle

	// callbacks are due: see tell

}
```

Group is a redundancy group in the sense of IEC 60870-5-104: several connections to one controlled station, of which exactly one has data transfer started. The others are established, stay in STOPDT and are supervised with test frames, ready to take over.

This is what the protocol offers in place of a connection pool. An IEC 60870-5-104 connection is not an interchangeable request channel: the station sends its spontaneous data on the one started connection, and sequence numbers, acknowledgements and command procedures belong to it. Opening more connections does not add throughput; it adds availability.

The group starts data transfer on the first connection that becomes established; when several are, on the one whose address comes first. When the active connection is lost it starts another one and re-establishes the lost one in the background as a standby. A path that returns does not take data transfer back by itself: see [Group.Switchover](#func-group-switchover). Every connection delivers to the same [Handler](#type-handler).

The request methods act on the active connection and fail with [iec104.ErrNotConnected](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrNotConnected) when there is none. A Group is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewGroup

```go
func NewGroup(addrs []string, opts ...Option) (*Group, error)
```

NewGroup returns a redundancy group over the given station addresses, which are typically two network paths to the same station or two redundant front ends. opts apply to every connection; [WithAutoStart](#func-withautostart) is controlled by the group and reconnection is always on ([WithReconnect](#func-withreconnect) sets its delays). The group is not connected until [Group.Connect](#func-group-connect) is called.

#### func (Group) Connect

```go

```

Connect establishes the connections and returns as soon as one of them has data transfer started. The others keep being established in the background, as does every connection that is lost later.

If no connection can be started before ctx ends, Connect returns an error that matches [iec104.ErrConnectFailed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrConnectFailed); the group keeps trying in the background until it is closed.

#### func (Group) Switchover

```go
func (g *Group) Switchover(ctx context.Context) error
```

Switchover moves data transfer from the active connection to the next established standby: STOPDT on the one, STARTDT on the other. It fails with [iec104.ErrNotConnected](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrNotConnected) when no standby is established, in which case the active connection is left as it is.

The switch handler has been told of the change when Switchover returns, and so have the state handlers, unless one of them is still busy with an earlier call. Switchover may be called from a handler; the handlers are then told after that handler has returned.


TestCommand sends a test command over the active connection. See [Client.TestCommand](#func-client-testcommand).

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	HandleASDU(a *asdu.ASDU)
}
```

Handler receives the ASDUs the controlled station sends.

HandleASDU is called from a single goroutine per connection, in the order the ASDUs arrived. A handler that blocks delays the delivery of everything that follows, including the answers other goroutines are waiting for.

It may call [Client.Send](#func-client-send), [Client.State](#func-client-state) and [Client.Close](#func-client-close). It must not call the request methods ([Client.Command](#func-client-command), [Client.Interrogate](#func-client-interrogate), [Client.Read](#func-client-read) and the like): their answers are delivered by the very goroutine the handler is running on, so they would only time out. Start a goroutine for work that needs them.

#### func WithASDUParams

```go
func WithASDUParams(p asdu.Params) Option
```

WithASDUParams overrides the ASDU layout. IEC 60870-5-104 fixes it to [asdu.IEC104](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#IEC104), so this is only needed for non-conformant devices or to set the time zone of time tags with [asdu.Params.In](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#Params.In).

#### func WithAutoStart

```go
func WithAutoStart(enabled bool) Option
```

WithAutoStart controls whether STARTDT is sent as part of connecting and reconnecting. Default true. Disable it for a redundant standby connection, which stays in STOPDT until [Client.StartDT](#func-client-startdt) is called.

```go
func WithDialer(d Dialer) Option
```

WithDialer replaces the transport dialer, for example to bind a local address, go through a proxy or connect over an in-memory pipe in tests. When combined with [WithTLS](#func-withtls) the TLS handshake runs on top of the connection the dialer returns.

WithHandler sets the receiver of ASDUs. Without one, received ASDUs are only visible through the request methods that collect them.


WithOriginator sets the originator address placed in ASDUs built by the client's request methods. Default 0.

#### func WithParams

```go
func WithParams(p apci.Params) Option
```

WithParams sets the protocol parameters k, w and t0..t3. Zero K, W, T0, T1 and T2 take their defaults; a zero T3 disables the idle test. The values must match the configuration of the controlled station.

#### func WithReconnect

```go
func WithReconnect(r Reconnect) Option
```

WithReconnect enables automatic reconnection: when an established connection is lost, the client re-dials with exponential backoff until it succeeds or is closed. Requests issued while disconnected fail with [iec104.ErrNotConnected](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrNotConnected). Zero fields of r take their defaults.

#### func WithRequestTimeout

```go
func WithRequestTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithRequestTimeout bounds how long a request method waits for the confirmation or the data it asked for when its context has no deadline. Default 10s. Zero or negative disables the bound. With [WithRetry](#func-withretry) it bounds every attempt, whatever the context.

#### func WithRetry

```go
func WithRetry(r Retry) Option
```

WithRetry makes the client repeat requests that are safe to repeat when they fail for a transient reason. Zero fields of r take their defaults.

Retried: [Client.Interrogate](#func-client-interrogate), [Client.CounterInterrogate](#func-client-counterinterrogate) with [asdu.FreezeRead](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#FreezeRead), [Client.Read](#func-client-read) and [Client.TestCommand](#func-client-testcommand). They only read from the station.

Never retried: [Client.Command](#func-client-command), [Client.Deactivate](#func-client-deactivate), [Client.ClockSync](#func-client-clocksync), [Client.ResetProcess](#func-client-resetprocess) and [Client.Send](#func-client-send). A command whose confirmation was lost may already have operated the process, and IEC 60870-5-104 has no way to ask; repeating it is the application's decision.

A request is repeated when the connection was lost or is not established, or when the station did not answer within the request timeout. It is not repeated when the station refused it ([\*iec104.NegativeError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#NegativeError)), when an identical request is pending or when the caller's context ended. Combine with [WithReconnect](#func-withreconnect): the backoff gives the client time to come back.

With retries enabled the request timeout bounds each attempt, also when the caller's context has a deadline; that deadline bounds the whole call.

#### func WithSecurity

```go
func WithSecurity(ep *sec.Endpoint) Option
```

WithSecurity applies the application-layer security of IEC 62351-5 (IEC TS 60870-5-7) to the connection: ep, which must have the role sec.Controlling, runs the Station Association and the Session Key Change when data transfer starts, and from then on every ASDU travels as Secure Data. [Client.Connect](#func-client-connect) returns once the secure session is established, or fails with the reason it could not be. Requests sent before that wait for it, within their timeout.

The clients of a [Group](#type-group) serve one controlled station and share one Endpoint: the station keeps one association per controlling station, and the connection with data transfer started carries it. Security can be combined with [WithTLS](#func-withtls).

#### func WithStartHandler

```go
func WithStartHandler(f func(ctx context.Context, c *Client)) Option
```

WithStartHandler registers a function that runs each time the client has established a connection and started data transfer on it: after [Client.Connect](#func-client-connect) and after every automatic reconnect. It is the place for what a controlling station does on a fresh connection, typically a general interrogation and a clock synchronization.

f runs on its own goroutine and may call any method of the client. ctx is cancelled when that connection ends or the client is closed.

#### func WithStateHandler

```go
func WithStateHandler(f func(state iec104.State, err error)) Option
```

WithStateHandler registers a callback for connection state changes. err is the reason when the state is [iec104.StateDisconnected](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#StateDisconnected) or a reconnect attempt failed, nil otherwise. Notifications are delivered one at a time, in order, and each state once: "disconnected" is the last thing a closed client reports.

The callback may call the client, [Client.Close](#func-client-close) included. It should return soon: the next notification waits for it, and so does a [Client.Close](#func-client-close) called from another goroutine.

#### func WithSwitchHandler

```go
func WithSwitchHandler(f func(active *Client)) Option
```

WithSwitchHandler registers a callback of a [Group](#type-group): it is called when another connection of the group becomes the active one, with that connection's client, or with nil when no connection is available any more. Calls are made one at a time and in order. The callback may call the group, [Group.Switchover](#func-group-switchover) and [Group.Close](#func-group-close) included, and should return soon: the next call waits for it. A plain [Client](#type-client) ignores the option.

#### func WithTLS

```go
func WithTLS(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

WithTLS secures the connection with TLS as profiled by IEC 62351-3. The conventional port is [apci.DefaultTLSPort](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/apci#DefaultTLSPort). If cfg.ServerName is empty it is taken from the address.

### type Reconnect

```go
type Reconnect struct {
	// MinDelay is the delay before the first attempt after a connection
	// was lost. Default 1s.
	MinDelay time.Duration
	// MaxDelay caps the exponential backoff between attempts. Default 30s.
	MaxDelay time.Duration
}
```

Reconnect configures automatic reconnection.

### type Retry

```go
type Retry struct {
	// Attempts is the total number of attempts, the first one included.
	// Default 3.
	Attempts int
	// Backoff is the delay before the second attempt; it doubles with
	// every further attempt. Default 500ms.
	Backoff time.Duration
	// MaxBackoff caps the delay. Default 10s.
	MaxBackoff time.Duration
}
```

Retry configures automatic retries of idempotent requests.
